title.en: Electric current, drift velocity and Ohm's law

hook.en: Electrons in a copper wire drift at about a millimetre per second, yet the bulb glows the instant you press the switch. The field travels almost at the speed of light and sets every electron drifting at once.
hook.kn: ತಾಮ್ರದ ತಂತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ಸೆಕೆಂಡಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು ಒಂದು ಮಿಲಿಮೀಟರ್ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಲೆಯುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದರೂ ಸ್ವಿಚ್ ಒತ್ತಿದ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಬಲ್ಬ್ ಉರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಡಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಒಮ್ಮೆಲೇ ಚಲಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Define current and drift velocity; use I = neAv_d.
State Ohm's law and relate resistance to resistivity.
Explain resistivity in terms of relaxation time.

narration.en: Electrons in a copper wire drift at about a millimetre per second, yet the bulb glows the instant you press the switch. The field travels almost at the speed of light and sets every electron drifting at once.
narration.kn: ತಾಮ್ರದ ತಂತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ಸೆಕೆಂಡಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು ಒಂದು ಮಿಲಿಮೀಟರ್ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಲೆಯುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದರೂ ಸ್ವಿಚ್ ಒತ್ತಿದ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಬಲ್ಬ್ ಉರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಡಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಒಮ್ಮೆಲೇ ಚಲಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge, I = dq/dt; unit ampere (1 A = 1 C s⁻¹). Conventional current is the direction of flow of positive charge. In a metal, free electrons move randomly; an applied field E gives them a small average drift velocity opposite to E: $v_d = eE\tau/m$, where τ is the average time between collisions (relaxation time). With n free electrons per m³ and cross-section A, $I = neAv_d$.
body.kn: ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಪ್ರವಾಹ I = dq/dt, ಏಕಮಾನ ಆಂಪಿಯರ್. ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವು ಮುಕ್ತ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಣ್ಣ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಅಲೆತದ ವೇಗ v_d = eEτ/m ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರವಾಹ I = neAv_d.

points.en: v_d = eEτ/m, opposite to E for electrons

narration.en: Current is charge per second. A field gives the free electrons a small average drift velocity, e E tau by m, opposite to the field. The current is n e A v d.

blocks.formula: I = n e A v_d,\qquad v_d = \frac{eE\tau}{m}

title.en: On the board: drift velocity and Ohm's law

narration.en: In a wire with a field E, free electrons drift slowly against E, while the current flows along E. In time Δt the electrons in a length v_d Δt cross a section, so the current is I = n e A v_d. Example: 1.5 A in copper of cross-section 10⁻⁷ m² gives a drift speed of only about 1.1 millimetre per second. Ohm's law: V is proportional to I, and the slope of the V–I line is the resistance R. R grows with length and falls with area: R = ρl/A, where ρ, the resistivity, depends on the material.

say.en: In a wire with a field E, free electrons drift slowly against E, while the current flows along E.
In time Δt the electrons in a length v_d Δt cross a section, so the current is I = n e A v_d.
Example: 1.5 A in copper of cross-section 10⁻⁷ m² gives a drift speed of only about 1.1 millimetre per second.
Ohm's law: V is proportional to I, and the slope of the V–I line is the resistance R.
R grows with length and falls with area: R = ρl/A, where ρ, the resistivity, depends on the material.

body.en: Ohm's law: at constant temperature the current in a conductor is proportional to the potential difference, V = IR. Resistance $R = \rho l/A$, where the resistivity $\rho = m/(ne^2\tau)$ depends only on the material and temperature, not on shape. In vector form, current density $j = I/A = \sigma E$, with conductivity σ = 1/ρ.
body.kn: ಓಮ್ ನಿಯಮ: ಸ್ಥಿರ ತಾಪದಲ್ಲಿ V = IR. ರೋಧ R = ρl/A; ರೋಧಶೀಲತೆ ρ = m/(ne²τ) ವಸ್ತು ಮತ್ತು ತಾಪವನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. j = σE.

narration.en: Ohm's law says V equals I R at constant temperature. Resistance is rho l by A, and resistivity rho depends only on the material and temperature.
narration.kn: ಓಮ್ ನಿಯಮ: ಸ್ಥಿರ ತಾಪದಲ್ಲಿ V = IR. ರೋಧ R = ρl/A; ರೋಧಶೀಲತೆ ρ = m/(ne²τ) ವಸ್ತು ಮತ್ತು ತಾಪವನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. j = σE.

caption.en: Drift speed v_d = I/(neA) for copper (n = 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³). The electrons crawl at millimetres per second, though the signal travels almost at the speed of light.

body.en: If a wire is stretched to n times its length with its volume unchanged, its resistance becomes n² times. If its radius is made 1/n times by drawing it out, the resistance becomes n⁴ times.
